name: Neptunium
occurrence: Found only in trace amounts naturally, as a product of uranium ore's neutron capture reactions; mainly produced artificially in nuclear reactors.
majorUses: Radioisotope thermoelectric generators for deep-space missions (neptunium-237 based, in newer NASA plutonium-238 production chains)
safetyNotes: Radioactive and requires controlled handling; produced and monitored under nuclear non-proliferation oversight given its role in some nuclear fuel cycles.
notableCharacteristics: The first transuranium element ever synthesized (the first element beyond uranium on the periodic table), continuing the 'named after planets' pattern since Neptune follows Uranus in the solar system.
whyHere: Sitting one proton beyond uranium, neptunium was the first element ever created that doesn't occur in meaningful natural quantities on Earth, produced instead by bombarding uranium with neutrons — a milestone that opened the door to the entire transuranium era of the periodic table.
didYouKnow: Neptunium's discovery in 1940 directly followed uranium's naming pattern — since Neptune is the next planet out from Uranus in the solar system, the newly created 'element 93' got an equally fitting name.
genZNote: First-ever manufactured element beyond uranium. Basically opened the door for the entire back half of the periodic table.
